hook.text: Every year, 24 billion tons of topsoil wash away globally. That's enough to fill 160 million train cars.

buildup.text: Raindrops hit bare soil at 20 mph, dislodging particles. Sheet flow carries them downhill.

discovery.text: Rills form first—tiny channels. Left unchecked, they become gullies that carve permanent scars in fields.

twist.text: Cover crops and mulch absorb raindrop impact. A simple plant cover stops most erosion before it starts.

climax.text: Soil erodes 10 to 100 times faster than it forms. We're spending a savings account we can't refill.

punchline.text: Rain builds soil over centuries. Rain destroys it in hours.

quiz.question: How much faster does soil erode compared to how quickly it forms?
